name: Graham Platner
role: Maine oysterman and Marine veteran; Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2026 until withdrawing in July 2026
summary: A progressive populist who campaigned on Medicare for All, taxes on billionaires, union rights, abortion rights and opposition to pointless wars. His past online posts and a skull tattoo drew controversy, and he apologized for the posts. He withdrew from the race in July 2026 after a sexual assault allegation that he denies.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Platform backs Medicare for All and calls health care a right.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Platform: raise the federal minimum wage and index it to inflation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Backs a billionaire minimum tax and a 5-6% wealth tax on wealth over $1bn.

unions-good.rationale: Platform backs the PRO Act and punishing illegal union-busting; says he wants to expand workers' right to organize.

regulate-corporations.rationale: His healthcare plan would ban insurers and private equity from owning medical practices and hospitals and break up healthcare monopolies, and his platform would break up monopolies generally.

strong-leader.rationale: His democracy plan says power has drifted to the executive and calls for reclaiming Congress's war powers and powers of the purse so executive power stays accountable.

limit-guns.rationale: At his April 2026 town hall he said he supports universal background checks and red flag laws that restrict firearms for people with a history of violence, adding that other steps must address poverty and mental healthcare.

reviewHistory.rationale: Mixed: supports universal background checks and red flag laws but opposes an assault weapons ban as proposed; owns AR-15s.

abortion-legal.rationale: Platform: supports a strong federal guarantee of the right to choose.

nation-first.rationale: In his Zero Hour interview he calls himself an internationalist, not an isolationist, who believes in international institutions and law.

open-borders.rationale: His platform says the country needs strong border security alongside a path to citizenship and 'we cannot do one without the other'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Platform calls for urgent climate action and stronger Clean Air and Clean Water Act enforcement; no specific drastic measures found.

tax-inheritance.rationale: His tax plan says the tax-free transfer of massive estates ('Buy-Borrow-Die') must end.

natural-rulers.rationale: His democracy plan says democracy is not rules handed down from elites but begins with the truth that all real power comes from the people.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Platform affirms Wabanaki sovereignty; land authority not specifically addressed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Platform opposes any federal support for private school vouchers (federal level only).

class-collaboration.rationale: In his Zero Hour interview he says politics is about power and that he is building an organized working class for the fights to come, running against the billionaire class.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: His platform's 'Equality for ALL' section rejects treating people unequally because of race, gender identity or sexual orientation.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Says the system is built to enrich the wealthy and that a billionaire class owns Washington; calls Democratic leadership unreliable.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His platform's 'Equality for ALL' section rejects using race, gender identity or sexual orientation as a punching bag and backs federal LGBTQ anti-discrimination legislation.

consent-of-governed.rationale: His democracy plan says democracy is not rules handed down from elites and that all real power comes from the people.

separated-powers.rationale: His democracy plan restates checks and balances so that no branch dominates, restoring Congress's power against the executive and the courts.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: His democracy plan criticises the Taft-Hartley Act for limiting workers' ability to organize and strike and calls for reviving the right to organize.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: His democracy plan says power in a democracy answers to the people, calls for ethics rules binding Supreme Court justices and for keeping executive power accountable.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Platform and a March 2026 statement call for federal LGBTQ anti-discrimination legislation, which matches the view that businesses open to the public must not discriminate and the law may require it. Stated for LGBTQ grounds only.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: His democracy plan calls for ending the executive's intrusion on Congress's powers of the purse and taxation.

corporate-influence.rationale: His corruption plan says Citizens United handed corporations and billionaires unrestricted power to buy elections and that wealthy donors expect a return on their investment.

job-guarantee.rationale: His democracy plan endorses an economic bill of rights including the right to a useful job at a living wage, to be made real by strong congressional action.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Asked in his Zero Hour interview whether the United States should obey international law and international courts, he answered 'Yes, without question'.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: In his Zero Hour interview he says he is not a pacifist and that a country needs to defend itself, wanting a robust navy built for national defence.

term-limits.rationale: His platform supports strong term limits for Congress, two terms in the Senate and six in the House, and says to hold politicians to their pledges.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: His tax plan says wealth should come from work, not the tax code, and would tax capital gains and dividends like wages ('reward work, not wealth').

constitutional-jury-trial.rationale: His democracy plan calls juries a democratic check on state power and says the decline of jury trials must be reversed, at state and federal level.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: He backs overturning Citizens United by a court or constitutional amendment, a ban on corporate PAC money for federal candidates, and says he takes only individual donations and labour PACs.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: His democracy plan endorses a Second Bill of Rights guaranteeing adequate food, clothing, a decent home, medical care and security in old age, sickness and unemployment.

notes: Most issue positions are from campaign platform pages and secondary summaries; many specific topics (Israel as a state, nuclear power, trade, culture-war statements) had no direct quote found and are null. Withdrew July 2026; platform positions are his last stated ones. Later pass 2026-11-14 (claude-sonnet-5-5): added his detailed policy plans (tax, democracy, healthcare, corruption, energy), the Zero Hour and New Yorker Radio Hour interviews and a town-hall record, searched by theme (economy, government, society, world, liberty, ecology, means). He has held no office, so there is no record; everything is his own words. His assault weapons ban remark rests on a secondary report (Bearing Arms quoting NewsCenterMaine) that was not used, so limit-guns rests on the town hall alone. He withdrew in July 2026.
